messages:
Maya R.: Quick heads-up — I hit a blocking repro when trying our sample app on Cloudflare Workers (edge). The JS SDK build with conditional exports + types refuses to import, throws: "TypeError: Invalid attempt to import under commonjs".
Jared H.: ugh. can you paste package.json exports block?
Maya R.: sure — minimal snippet: ```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "require": "./dist/redwood.cjs",
    "import": "./dist/redwood.mjs",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./*": "./dist/*"
}
```
Priya S.: edge runtimes (workers/deno) only accept ESM, but the bundler/cloudflare sometimes resolves to the cjs entry if conditional exports aren't recognized. Might be a publish-metadata mismatch.
Maya R.: repro steps: 1) clone sample-app (link) 2) yarn && yarn build 3) deploy to workers — instant error at runtime. Locally with node 18 works fine.
Sam L.: do we generate both cjs + esm artifacts from the build? also what about the "type" field in package.json? if we set "type":"module" consumers break for cjs consumers.
Alex P.: we currently ship both builds from rollup: dist/redwood.cjs (cjs), dist/redwood.mjs (esm) and dist/index.d.ts. package.json has "type": "commonjs" right now.
Maya R.: CI publishes package fine but the sample-app's auto-deploy to edge uses esbuild + a worker bundler that reads package exports wrong. I'm seeing the bundler pick the cjs file and then runtime throws because Workers don't support require.
Jared H.: quick workaround for sample-app: pin to the mjs file via import like `import client from 'redwood/dist/redwood.mjs'` — but obviously can't ask everyone to do that.
Priya S.: Could this be because the package's exported "types" points to a single file rather than using the conditional exports for types? Some tools (tsserver/deno) read exports differently. Try: ```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "require": "./dist/redwood.cjs",
    "import": "./dist/redwood.mjs",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  },
  "types": {"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"},
  "./*": "./dist/*"
}
```
Sam L.: Hmm adding a top-level explicit types export might help TS, but not the runtime picking cjs. The root cause may be certain bundlers don't fully evaluate the conditions and fallback to require.
Dev SDK Bot: NOTE: A canary published as `redwood@canary-edge-fix` with a tweak to package.json exports is available for testing.
Maya R.: tried canary — good news, Workers deploy without the require error! :tada: But two issues remain: 1) some downstream bundlers still prefer the cjs path (rollup-plugin-node-resolve?) 2) types in editors sometimes point to dist/index.d.ts incorrectly when using path imports.
Jared H.: action items: 1) improve publish step to add explicit conditional export for types and an export for "default" that prefers import; 2) add note in sample-app onboarding doc about edge pinning/repro; 3) run quick fuzz against common bundlers (esbuild/webpack/rollup/deno) in CI.
Priya S.: I'll open a tiny PR to update package.json + publish CI job for canary. Also adding a small smoke test that deploys sample-app to a Workers preview action.
Alex P.: can we also add a small runtime check in the SDK that throws a helpful error when loaded via CJS in an ESM-only runtime? That would make the failure clearer for users.
Maya R.: yes please. current error is opaque. If SDK can detect environment and hint: "this build requires ESM — import the .mjs entry or upgrade bundler" it's much friendlier.
Sam L.: I'll add a note to the SDK migration doc and a quick example of `import client from 'redwood'` vs `const client = require('redwood').default` edge pitfalls.
Maya R.: thanks — once PR lands I'll re-run sample-app e2e and mark onboarding ticket done if green. :thumbsup:
Jared H.: thanks all — filing a short postmortem in ENG SDK board with triage and follow-ups.
